facts.statement: four official JavaScript files on Level Infinite's CDN contained attacker code.
The NIKKE PC launcher loads these files.
the attacker could run any command on your machine, read any file and take screenshots.
None of this undoes anything on machines that were already infected.
Both can delete files that show whether the agent ran.
This report comes from one infected machine, plus findings from other victims posted in the comments.
before reopening it, players should back up Launcher\intl_service\debug.log and tbs_cache
change passwords and other sensitive credentials from a clean device.
collect NIKKE account credentials, and steal information stored in web browsers.
Nikke has released an update with instructions on how to check computers for compromise.

editorial.title: NIKKE PC launcher compromise exposes a trusted CDN delivery path
editorial.summary: MotherSphere’s NIKKE investigation describes tampered scripts on Level Infinite’s CDN loading a remote-control agent. Follow-up reporting describes credential-stealing capabilities and warns that updated launcher cleanup can erase evidence of an earlier infection.
editorial.why_it_matters: Cleaning the delivery scripts does not undo an earlier infection. The research draws on an infected machine and attributed user reports; it does not establish how many players were affected.
editorial.action: Preserve launcher logs and caches before reopening the PC launcher. Then follow the publisher’s security-check guidance and reset exposed passwords and credentials from a clean device.
